gas_pipelines.title: Natural gas pipelines (operating)
gas_pipelines.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Natural Gas Interstate and Intrastate Pipelines map layer
gas_pipelines.licence: Public domain (U.S. Government work, U.S. Energy Information Administration); modified by Enerdatics (operating segments only, filed by state, simplified, fields reduced); no warranty
gas_pipelines.notes: EIA's pipeline layer has no capacity, diameter or throughput field: only pipe type, operator and status. Operating pipelines only; planned pipelines are not included. id = row number in the EIA source file, not stable across releases.
gas_pipelines.id_basis: source row number (1-based); stable within one release, not across releases

info.offshore_basis: touches no US state polygon and no non-US land polygon (countries input)
info.note: Counts above are per unique segment. A segment crossing a state border is written, whole, into every state file it touches; dedupe by id when merging files. id is the segment's row number in the EIA source file: stable within one release, NOT across releases. offshore = the segment touches no Census (coast-clipped) state polygon and no non-US land, and is filed under the nearest state (within 250 km); a segment on non-US land only (Canada, Mexico) is dropped and counted as outside_us_land. length_km is geodesic (WGS84) on the unsimplified segment.

info.note: Counts above are per feature. A feature crossing a state border is written, whole, into every state file it touches; dedupe by id when merging files. id is the feature's row number in the GEM extract (it carries no GEM project id): stable within one extract, NOT across releases. A feature on non-US land only is dropped (outside_us_land). One project can be several features (segments) with the same pipeline_name. capacity_bcm_y = GEM capacity in billion cubic metres per year (blank where GEM has none). length_km is geodesic (WGS84) on the unsimplified route; routes are approximate.

plants.title: Existing conventional power plants (EIA-860M)
plants.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-860M Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory (September 2026), Operating and Planned tabs incl. Puerto Rico
plants.licence: Public domain. Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-860M (September 2026)
plants.modifications: Modified by Enerdatics: generator rows aggregated to one point per plant and status (operating / planned); conventional plants only (plants mainly solar, wind or battery storage left out); retired and canceled generators excluded; fields reduced; coordinates rounded; no warranty
plants.vintage: EIA-860M, September 2026 (generator inventory as of that month)
plants.coverage_basis: national dataset: a state without a file has no plants in it

excluded_solar_wind_battery_plants.rule: solar, wind and battery plants excluded: a plant is left out when its largest fuel category by summed nameplate MW is solar, wind or battery storage, even if it also has a conventional unit

info.note: Conventional plants only. One point per plant and status group, aggregated from generator rows: a plant with operating units and a planned expansion appears twice (status operating / planned). fuel_category is the plant's largest category by summed nameplate MW (ties: more generators, then the order of fuel_categories); technology and energy_source are the largest within it. nameplate_mw and generators count only the conventional units; has_renewable_units = the plant also has solar, wind or battery units, not counted. planned_operation = the earliest planned operation year-month among the plant's planned generators. Rows without usable coordinates or state are dropped and counted per reason.
